User.title: User
User.description: Represents a member of the St. John Chrysostom Bookclub, including their personal details, progress metrics, and administrative attributes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

name.description: The full name of the user.

email.description: The user's email address, used for contact and display purposes. (Not for authentication credentials)

profilePictureUrl.description: URL to the user's uploaded profile picture.

batchYear.description: The year or batch identifier when the user joined the bookclub.

readingLevel.description: A descriptive level indicating the user's reading proficiency or engagement (e.g., 'Beginner', 'Intermediate', 'Advanced').

points.description: The total cumulative points earned by the user.

level.description: The current achievement level of the user based on points or engagement.

streak.description: The current consecutive daily reading streak of the user.

status.description: The active status of the user (e.g., 'Active', 'Inactive').

role.description: The role of the user within the bookclub (e.g., 'member', 'admin').

Book.title: Book
Book.description: Represents a book that is or has been part of the bookclub's reading plan.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Book entity.

description.description: A brief summary or description of the book.

totalPages.description: The total number of pages in the book.

currentReadingPlanDueDate.description: The due date for completing this book within the current bookclub reading plan. (Optional)

Challenge.title: Challenge
Challenge.description: Defines a specific task or goal that members can undertake to earn points and engage with the club's activities.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Challenge entity.

description.description: A detailed description of the challenge and its objectives.

pointsReward.description: The number of points awarded upon successful completion of the challenge.

completionCriteria.description: Description of what needs to be done to complete the challenge (e.g., 'Read 10 pages', 'Answer 3 questions').

startDate.description: The date and time when the challenge becomes active.

endDate.description: The date and time when the challenge expires.

type.description: The category or type of challenge (e.g., 'Daily', 'Weekly', 'Special').

isActive.description: Indicates if the challenge is currently active and available to members.

UserChallenge.title: UserChallenge
UserChallenge.description: Tracks a specific member's participation and progress on a particular challenge.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserChallenge entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User participating in the challenge. (Relationship: User 1:N UserChallenge)

challengeId.description: Reference to the Challenge being undertaken. (Relationship: Challenge 1:N UserChallenge)

status.description: The current status of the user's challenge (e.g., 'Pending', 'InProgress', 'Completed', 'Failed').

startedAt.description: The date and time when the user started the challenge.

completedAt.description: The date and time when the user completed the challenge. Null if not completed.

progress.description: A textual or numerical representation of the user's progress within the challenge (e.g., '3/10 pages read').

pointsEarned.description: The actual points earned by the user for this specific completion, reflecting the challenge's reward at the time of completion.

Discussion.title: Discussion
Discussion.description: Represents a scheduled discussion event for members, often related to a specific book or topic.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Discussion entity.

bookId.description: Reference to the Book this discussion is about. (Optional. Relationship: Book 1:N Discussion)

topic.description: The main topic of the discussion.

scheduledDateTime.description: The date and time when the discussion is scheduled.

isActive.description: Indicates if the discussion is currently active or upcoming.

organizerId.description: Reference to the User who organized the discussion. (Optional. Relationship: User 1:N Discussion)

Notification.title: Notification
Notification.description: Represents a system-generated alert or message sent to a specific user within the application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Notification entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User who is the recipient of the notification. (Relationship: User 1:N Notification)

type.description: The type of event that triggered the notification (e.g., 'LevelUp', 'NewChallenge', 'ChallengeCompleted', 'DiscussionScheduled', 'NudgeReceived', 'StreakWarning').

message.description: The content of the notification message.

relatedEntityType.description: The type of entity related to this notification (e.g., 'Challenge', 'Discussion', 'Nudge'). Optional.

relatedEntityId.description: The ID of the entity related to this notification. Optional.

isRead.description: Indicates whether the user has read the notification.

createdAt.description: The date and time when the notification was created.

expiresAt.description: The date and time when the notification is set to expire and disappear (e.g., 48 hours after creation).

Nudge.title: Nudge
Nudge.description: Represents an encouragement message sent from one member to another to motivate reading or challenge completion.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Nudge entity.

senderId.description: Reference to the User who sent the nudge. (Relationship: User 1:N Nudge - as sender)

receiverId.description: Reference to the User who received the nudge. (Relationship: User 1:N Nudge - as receiver)

message.description: The encouragement message sent with the nudge.

sentAt.description: The date and time when the nudge was sent.

isBonusAwarded.description: Indicates if the nudger received bonus points for the receiver completing reading within 24 hours.

bonusAwardedAt.description: The date and time when the bonus points were awarded, if applicable. Null if not awarded.

UserReadingProgress.title: UserReadingProgress
UserReadingProgress.description: Tracks an individual member's progress through a specific book.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserReadingProgress entity.

userId.description: Reference to the User whose reading progress is being tracked. (Relationship: User 1:N UserReadingProgress)

bookId.description: Reference to the Book being read. (Relationship: Book 1:N UserReadingProgress)

currentPage.description: The last page number the user has read in this book.

startedReadingAt.description: The date and time when the user started reading this book.

lastReadAt.description: The most recent date and time the user updated their reading progress for this book.

isCompleted.description: Indicates if the user has completed reading this book.

completedAt.description: The date and time when the user marked the book as completed. Null if not completed.

AdminActionLog.title: AdminActionLog
AdminActionLog.description: Records administrative actions performed by users with 'admin' roles for auditing purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AdminActionLog entity.

adminId.description: Reference to the User (admin) who performed the action. (Relationship: User 1:N AdminActionLog)

actionType.description: The type of administrative action performed (e.g., 'adjust_points', 'reset_streak', 'assign_role', 'create_book', 'edit_challenge', 'create_discussion').

targetEntityType.description: The type of entity that was affected by the action (e.g., 'User', 'Book', 'Challenge', 'Discussion').

targetEntityId.description: The ID of the specific entity that was affected by the action.

details.description: A descriptive message or JSON string containing details of the change (e.g., old value, new value).

timestamp.description: The date and time when the administrative action was performed.

definition.description: Collection storing user profiles. Each document is uniquely identified by the user's Firebase Authentication UID. Includes denormalized 'role' for application logic and general user details. Ownership is path-based, meaning a user can only read/write their own document.

Dedicated collection for identifying administrators. The document ID (`adminId`) corresponds to a user's UID. The *existence* of a document at this path signifies an admin role. This enables secure and simple DBAC (Database-Based Access Control) rules for admin-only operations by checking for document existence. Documents in this collection can be empty or contain minimal metadata, but their primary purpose is authorization via presence.

params.name: adminId
params.description: The unique identifier (UID) of the user who has an 'admin' role.

params.name: bookId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific book.

definition.description: Global collection for all challenges available to members. Accessible by all authenticated members for viewing. Admin users have privileges to create, edit, and delete documents in this collection.

params.name: challengeId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific challenge.

definition.description: Global collection for all scheduled discussion events. Accessible by all authenticated members for viewing. Admin users have privileges to create, edit, and delete documents in this collection.

params.name: discussionId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific discussion event.

definition.description: Subcollection tracking a specific user's participation in challenges. Ownership is determined by the `userId` in the path, ensuring Authorization Independence. A user can only access their own userChallenge documents.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who owns this challenge progress.

params.name: userChallengeId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific user's challenge progress record.

definition.description: Subcollection for system-generated notifications specific to each user. Ownership is determined by the `userId` in the path, ensuring Authorization Independence. Notifications include an `expiresAt` field for automated disappearance after 48 hours.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who is the recipient of this notification.

params.name: notificationId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific notification.

definition.description: Subcollection storing nudges sent by a specific user. This denormalized path allows the sender to easily retrieve their nudge history, ensuring Authorization Independence for the sender. When a nudge is created, a document is also created in the receiver's `receivedNudges` subcollection.

params.name: senderId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who sent the nudge.

params.name: nudgeId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific nudge instance.

definition.description: Subcollection storing nudges received by a specific user. This denormalized path allows the receiver to easily retrieve their received nudges, ensuring Authorization Independence for the receiver. When a nudge is created, a document is also created in the sender's `sentNudges` subcollection.

params.name: receiverId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who received the nudge.

params.name: nudgeId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific nudge instance.

definition.description: Subcollection tracking an individual member's progress for specific books. Ownership is determined by the `userId` in the path, ensuring Authorization Independence. A user can only access their own reading progress records.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user whose reading progress is being tracked.

params.name: userReadingProgressId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific user's reading progress record for a book.

definition.description: Global collection for auditing administrative actions. Only users with the 'admin' role (verified by `/roles_admin/{adminId}`) can read or write to this collection, ensuring a homogeneous security posture and easy querying for audit purposes.

params.name: adminActionLogId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific administrative action log entry.

firestore.reasoning:
The recommended Firestore structure prioritizes Authorization Independence and Structural Segregation to ensure robust, debuggable security rules and efficient data access. 

**Authorization Independence (Denormalization Strategy):**

1.  **User-Owned Data:** For entities strictly owned by a user (e.g., `UserChallenge`, `Notification`, `UserReadingProgress`), the `userId` is embedded directly into the collection path (e.g., `/users/{userId}/notifications/{notificationId}`). This makes the owner explicit in the path, allowing security rules to simply check `request.auth.uid == userId` without needing any `get()` operations, which would break atomic writes and complicate rule debugging. This strategy is foundational for secure and scalable user-specific data.

2.  **Nudging Feature (`Nudge`):** To manage nudges where both the sender and receiver need access (e.g., sender views 'sent' history, receiver views 'received' nudges), the `Nudge` entity is denormalized into two user-specific subcollections: `/users/{senderId}/sentNudges/{nudgeId}` and `/users/{receiverId}/receivedNudges/{nudgeId}`. When a nudge is created, a single logical nudge is represented by two physical documents (one in each subcollection). This ensures that a user can easily list their sent or received nudges without complex queries or cross-document `get()` calls in security rules. Rules can simply check `request.auth.uid == senderId` for sent nudges and `request.auth.uid == receiverId` for received nudges, maintaining authorization independence.

3.  **Global Roles (Admin Access):** Administrative access is handled by a dedicated top-level collection, `/roles_admin/{adminId}`. An admin's UID will exist as a document ID in this collection. Security rules can check for the *existence* of `request.auth.uid` in this collection (`exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid))`). This is a highly efficient and secure `DBAC` (Database-Based Access Control) pattern, avoiding custom claims and complex role lookups.

**Querying for Authorization Purposes (QAPs):**

All collections are structured to directly support Query-as-Permission (QAP). This means that a client-side query for data should inherently only return data the user is authorized to see, without the need for `where` clauses that security rules would have to filter. 

*   **User-Specific Data:** Queries like `db.collection('users').doc(auth.currentUser.uid).collection('notifications').get()` inherently filter by the authenticated user's ID, fulfilling QAP. The security rules then only need to verify that `userId` in the path matches `request.auth.uid`.
*   **Global Data (`Books`, `Challenges`, `Discussions`):** These are top-level collections accessible (likely read-only) by all authenticated members. This provides a homogeneous security posture for all documents within these collections, simplifying rules. Admin actions on these are controlled by the `/roles_admin` collection.
*   **Admin Logs (`AdminActionLog`):** This collection is a global log but secured such that only authenticated administrators (as determined by `/roles_admin`) can read or write to it, ensuring QAP for administrative oversight.
